page.overview:
Who is Gyyagin?

Gyyagin is a fictional monster created by Stephen King for his short story "Jerusalem's Lot". A giant extraterrestrial worm that transforms its human followers into undead servitors, Gyyagin is itself identified as a servant of "Yogsoggoth" (possibly Yog-Sothoth), and is heavily implied to be the titular Worm that the grimoire known as De Vermis Mysteriis (English: Mysteries of the Worm) alludes to.

Gyyagin is a massive worm that burrows under the ground in the area around the town of Jerusalem's Lot, Maine. Descriptors and sobriquets include "the Worm from beyond space", "Star-Eater" and "Blinder of Time". Its body is segmented, at least 5 ft. wide, grey in colour, and produces black slime as it moves around its tunnels. Wherever it crawls over, the ground's vegetation withers and turns white. Its mere proximity seems to have a noxious effect on the local inhabitants, precipitating the birth of eyeless or noseless children.

Like many Mythos deities, Gyyagin demands bloody sacrifices. Its victims are apparently killed by constriction, as the gargantuan worm squeezes them until their blood vessels are ruptured.

Gyyagin is perhaps most notable for transforming its human followers into undead creatures (referred to at one point as nosferatu) which live in its tunnels with it. Blood relatives of these cultists seem to be subtly attracted to the area that the Worm inhabits, but it is not known whether this psychic link is formed by Gyyagin or by the undead relatives themselves.
